_comment: Dandisets that are counted as one dataset when measuring how often the
Some datasets are released as several dandisets that share a primary paper
or a source, and papers reusing them often cannot be told apart. A paper
that reused one of them is proposed for all of them, and the reviewer calls
the one it used Reuse and the rest Neither. Counted pair by pair, every
such paper adds one confirmation and several rejections, although the
classifier was right that the paper reused the data.
When measuring precision, the pairs one paper has with the dandisets of a
group are therefore counted once, as reuse if any of them is. Reviews and
the per-dandiset record in confirmed_reuse.json are unaffected, so a paper
is still credited to the dandiset the reviewer named.
Each group gives the reason, so it can be re-examined if the dandisets are
later consolidated or come to be told apart reliably.

reason: The maze-reaching recordings of Churchland et al. 2010 and 2012:
